#### *Part 4* Name FOUR structures which could be damaged by inserting the needle TOO FAR, when using the approach shown above.

1.  Carotid artery
2.  Cervical sympathetic chain
3.  Vagus Nerve
4.  Pleura / Pneumothorax
5.  Thoracic duct (left IJ approach)

#### *Part 5* The following chest x-ray shows a central line in situ. Name the blood vessel traversed by the central line at points A, B and C.

![](/content/exams/anzca/2017/A/1/standard-image28.png){fig-alt="Chest radiograph with central line and structures A, B, C and X"}

#### *Part 6* Name the cardiac structure labelled X. 

A: left internal jugular vein B: left brachiocephalic Vein C: Superior vena cava, X: right Atrium 

#### *Part 7* What criteria do you use to assess the position of the tip of a central line on a chest x-ray?

The CVC tip should be level with the carina and above the cavo-atrial junction
